authors: Armin Piwek, Mark de Vries, Jan Grajczak, Hendrik Wester, Norman Mohnfeld, Christian Nowroth, Julius Peddinghaus, Sarah Seffer, Jörg Hermsdorf, Stefan Kaierle, Jens Twiefel, Jörg Wallaschek, Kai Brunotte, Bernd-Arno Behrens
name: luh-tf_hollow-forward-extrusion-stainless-steel-nickel-based-alloy
notes: Combining different materials enables the fabrication of load-adapted areas, expanding the limited potential of monolithic components. One innovative approach to manufacture hybrid high-performance components is Tailored Forming. This process chain involves an initial joining step to create a material bond, followed by a forming step to modify the joint. In this study, cost-effective and corrosion-resistant stainless steel EN 1.4301 (AISI 304) is combined with the thermally high-strength nickel-based Alloy 625 using either rotary friction welding, conventional or ultrasonic-assisted laser beam welding. Subsequently, hollow forward extrusion is conducted to enhance bond properties through thermo-mechanical treatment of the joining zone. The effects of different joining methods on formability are analysed through recorded process forces and micrographs. Additionally, finite element simulation is used to analyse the forming process in regard to material flow and stress distribution under variation of the forming sequence. Ultrasonic-assistance of laser beam welding effectively mitigates hardness gradients usually accruing and enables defect-free forming comparable to rotary friction welding, thereby expanding the applicability of fusion-based joining in Tailored Forming without the typical weakening of the strength profile at the centre of the specimen. However, this improvement is accompanied by a slight increase in peak forming force compared to rotary friction welding.
title: Hollow Forward Extrusion of Hybrid Components Made of Stainless Steel and Nickel-Based Alloy
